description: Who decided, and when (CP-AUTHOR-1; backlog #65 and #66). The schema leaves `provenance`, a Deviation's `decided` and `review-due` and an authorization's `date` optional; the validator REPORTS what is missing and fails nothing unless asked to. `author-vectors`: each case is a mini-bundle; `expected` is the report, one entry [rule, object id, count] per object and rule, in the order of the object ids by UTF-16 code unit (the order of the canonical form, RFC 8785; it differs from the order by code point for characters beyond U+FFFF) and, for one object, of the rules as listed here: AUTHOR-1 asks a Tailoring at consumer tier for the author of each select, exclude and operation (its own provenance, else the Tailoring's; count = entries without either), AUTHOR-2 asks a Risk, a Finding and an Implementation for provenance, AUTHOR-3 asks an approved or withdrawn Deviation for `decided` (count = Deviations), AUTHOR-4 asks an authorization for its date (count = authorizations). `review-vectors`: REVIEW-1 with the date given in `as-of`; `expected-overdue` and `expected-not-evaluable` list [object id, where], absent means empty. A point in time has passed when its UTC calendar day is before `as-of`; a duration counts from `decided`, else `opened`, on a Deviation and from `acceptance.date` on a Risk; a calendar period is not evaluated. Only an approved Deviation and a Risk still managed are asked. The messages are not part of the assertion.

author-vectors.name: a-consumer-tailoring-without-any-author
author-vectors.reason: one select and two operations, no provenance on any of them and none on the Tailoring; the Requirement and the Set are the authority's and are not asked

author-vectors.name: the-tailoring-names-its-author-once
author-vectors.reason: an entry without provenance has its Tailoring's: one person's Tailoring names that person once

author-vectors.name: an-entry-with-its-own-author-is-not-counted
author-vectors.reason: the first operation names its author; the select and the second operation have none and the Tailoring gives them none

author-vectors.name: an-authority's-own-tailoring-is-not-asked
author-vectors.reason: its id has the origin of the content it selects: authority-claimed. Duties bind at consumer tier (D13); the publisher is the author

author-vectors.name: a-predicate-select-is-counted
author-vectors.reason: a predicate select blocks the authority claim, so the Tailoring is a consumer's

author-vectors.name: a-soft-hyphen-in-the-origin-makes-a-consumer-who-is-asked
author-vectors.reason: the id differs from the content's origin by U+00AD; compared code point by code point it is a consumer's Tailoring (D2; backlog #58)

author-vectors.name: a-risk-a-finding-and-an-implementation-without-provenance
author-vectors.reason: one line per object, in the order of the ids

author-vectors.name: a-rating's-author-does-not-stand-for-the-risk
author-vectors.reason: inheritance runs from the record to the decision inside it, not back

author-vectors.name: a-decided-deviation-without-the-day-it-was-decided
author-vectors.reason: approved and withdrawn are decisions; pending is not one yet; the fourth says when

author-vectors.name: an-authority's-deviation-is-asked-too
author-vectors.reason: AUTHOR-3 is about the Deviation, whoever holds it

author-vectors.name: what-the-rules-do-not-ask
author-vectors.reason: a Requirement and a Set are attributed by their origin; a Mapping, a Check, an Assessment and an Attestation say who and when in fields their shape requires; a Component without an authorization holds no decision

author-vectors.name: ids-in-the-order-of-their-utf-16-code-units
author-vectors.reason: U+1F600 is written as the surrogate pair D83D DE00 and comes before U+E000 by code unit, after it by code point. The report follows the canonical form (RFC 8785), which orders by code unit; so a tool in a language that sorts strings by code point has to say so

review-vectors.name: a-date-time-is-read-in-utc
review-vectors.reason: 23:30 at UTC-5 on the 12th is 04:30 UTC on the 13th: due today

review-vectors.name: a-date-time-east-of-utc
review-vectors.reason: 00:30 at UTC+2 on the 13th is 22:30 UTC on the 12th

review-vectors.name: a-duration-counts-from-the-day-it-was-decided
review-vectors.reason: opened on the 1st, decided on the 10th: 48 hours from the start of the 10th end at the start of the 12th

review-vectors.name: a-calendar-period-is-not-evaluated
review-vectors.reason: D9: a calendar duration fails closed without the named calendar, and this tool has none

review-vectors.name: a-day-that-is-not-in-the-calendar
review-vectors.reason: the schema's pattern admits the 31st of any month; no day is invented for it

review-vectors.name: a-duration-in-seconds
review-vectors.reason: 86,400 seconds from the start of the 10th end at the start of the 11th

review-vectors.name: a-duration-that-ends-within-a-day
review-vectors.reason: 36 hours from the start of the 10th end at noon on the 11th; the day it falls on is the 11th, not the 12th
